content:
maya: seeing repeated RDMA resets on g5-multi-job-27 in us-west-2, started ~09:05 UTC. NCCL jobs hang, then the node drops into degraded mode. logs show ibv errors and kernel drops. anyone else?

infra-bot: Alert: RoCE fabric flapping detected on leaf-12 port-7 (2026-03-18T09:06:12Z) — packet-loss spike and qp errors.

chris: can you paste the ibverbs/dmesg snippets?

maya: sure — short extract: 
```
[  612.345678] mlx5_core 0000:09:00.0: QP 0x3f7 state changed to ERR (syndrome 0x20)
[  612.346012] ibmv: communication error, retrying...
[  613.001223] mlx5_core 0000:09:00.0: hw error: QP 0x3f7 rnr_timeout
```
and from containerized job logs: 
```
NCCL INFO Call to barrier timed out, attempted 120s
ibv_rc_pingpong: send completion w/ errno 104 (Connection reset by peer)
```

devon: classic RDMA remote resets. initial suspects: MTU mismatch somewhere, ECN/DSCP queuing, or a bad NIC firmware on leaf-12. Did you confirm MTU end-to-end?

maya: host MTU is 9000, container veth got 1500 for some pods, but we use host networking for these GPU jobs. I ran `ip -s link show` and leaf port shows 9000.

chris: can you run `ethtool -S eth0` on the host and `ibv_devinfo -vv`? also check switch counters (if accessible) for rx_dropped or palletized fragments.

maya: pasted outputs: 
```
# ibv_devinfo -vv
hca_id: mlx5_0
firmware: 21.34.1020
max_qp: 1048576
port 1: state: ACTIVE
link_layer: ETH, mtu: 4096
# ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "tx_dropped|rx_dropped|rx_fragment"
rx_dropped: 0
tx_dropped: 12
rx_fragmented: 0
```

lia: odd that mtu shows 4096 at verbs layer but host link is 9000. Could be VLAN/encap on the path (vxlan/overlay adding overhead) causing RoCE frames to exceed MTU and dropped later. Also seen fragmentation when offloads differ.

sam: FYI we had a switch firmware push last night to spine-b that touched headroom. Might be related — I'll check change log.

chris: also look for ARP/ND rediscovery storms — if a leaf is flapping, kernel may reset QPs when path changes. Run `netstat -s | grep -i arp` and `ip -s neigh show nud` to see churn.

maya: `ip -s neigh` shows a lot of REACHABLE->STALE transitions on 10.2.x.x between leaf-12 and spine-4. snippet: 
```
10.2.34.1 dev eth0 lladdr 00:aa:bb:cc:dd:ee REACHABLE 1m
10.2.34.2 dev eth0 lladdr 00:aa:bb:cc:dd:ff STALE 0
```

devon: that supports days theory — path flaps cause RDMA QPs to go ERR. Two tracks: 1) validate L2 path stability and MTU with switch counters + tcpdump mirrored on NIC to see oversized frames, 2) test direct ibv_rc_pingpong between devices across affected leaf/spine to reproduce.

maya: started a pingpong test now between node A and B (same rack) and got intermittent `send completion errno 104`. ran `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/rdma-capture.pcap` for 2 mins. uploading.

chris: good. while capture is running, collect switch counters for the exact ports (leaf-12:7 and spine-4:22). I asked infra-ops to pull hardware counters and fabric logs — they might show drops at ingress due to headroom accounting after firmware change.

infra-bot: infra-ops ticket created: #INFRA-1829 — investigating switch firmware impact.

lia: one more thing — check NIC offloads: `ethtool -k eth0` and ensure GSO/TSO and GRO are consistent; mismatches have caused L3 frames to be mis-sized for RoCE translations before.

maya: `ethtool -k` results: 
```
features for eth0:
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tso: on
gso: on
sg: on
```

devon: If contrast between HCA MTU 4096 and host 9000 is real, we need to check Mellanox MLX5 kernel module params — sometimes driver sets path MTU lower for RoCE v2 UDP encapsulation. Run `dmesg | grep -i mlx5` and `sysctl net.core.rmem_max` to ensure buffers aren't being starved.

maya: dmesg few more lines: 
```
mlx5_core 0000:09:00.0: RoCE v2 UDP offload enabled, max payload 3896
mlx5_core 0000:09:00.0: port 1: MTU configured 4096, link mtu 9000
```

chris: aha — driver offload reducing RoCE payload to 3896, that plus overlay add could exceed underlying path MTU. patch path: try forcing HCA MTU to 1500 temporarily (or adjust UDP offload) to see if error stops, or set host to 4096 via `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 4096` across path. But coordinate with infra-ops and SRE because changing host MTU can affect other traffic.

sam: switch team confirmed yesterday's change adjusted buffer thresholds. rolling back to previous profile for spine-4/leaf-12 now (in progress).

maya: thanks — I'll keep pingpong running and report back. currently scaling down affected TensorFlow job to reduce risk.

lia: once switch rollback finishes, re-run `ibv_rc_pingpong` and check NCCL tests. If fixed, we should push a driver/firmware compatibility note in infra runbook.

chris: sounds good. add a quick test to our GPU onboarding checklist: verify verbs MTU vs host MTU and confirm UDP offload settings.

maya: update — infra ops rolled back buffer profile -> I see much lower rx errors and QPs recovered, NCCL job resumed. keeping an eye for 30m. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INFRA-1829 updated: status -> investigating -> mitigated (rollback applied)

sam: filing follow-up for next week to test firmware + buffer profile together in staging before prod pushes.

maya: thanks all. keeping this thread pinned until we close the ticket.
